definitions.hard_technical_limit: Constraint imposed by finite resources, physical distance, or a stated protocol/resource model. Software may improve efficiency or choose trade-offs, not remove the constraint.
definitions.operational_pain: Documented failure mode or delivery friction with existing technical approaches; prevalence and commercial demand require customer validation.
definitions.market_gap: Evidence of unmet integration, tooling, pricing, portability or workflow demand. A market gap does not establish willingness to pay or absence of competitors.
definitions.speculative_claim: A proposal or forecast without deployment evidence. Every Keddeh/BRAINK intervention in this register remains a hypothesis.
definitions.distinct_sector: A separately addressable failure mechanism, buyer outcome and acceptance test. Related sectors may share infrastructure, but retain distinct IDs, delivery owners and independent analyst teams.

normalization_rules: One bottleneck_id maps to one proposed sector_id, one delivery_team_id and a separate analyst_team_id.
Sector names are proposals, not assertions that teams, products or deployments already exist.
Problem metrics are measurements to collect; all numerical acceptance thresholds are proposed pilot gates, not published Keddeh results.
Source publication dates are exact only where verified. Undated living documentation is marked undated and carries an access date.
Foundational sources establish mechanisms, not 2026 prevalence. Surveys describe their respondent samples, not all enterprises.
No aggregate market-size or universal exhaustive-coverage claim is made.
Existing tools are genuine alternatives; Keddeh must outperform or usefully integrate them rather than rebrand them.

analyst_control.separation: Each sector has a distinct analyst team identity and mandate. Delivery experts do not approve their own results.
required_outputs: Source and claim ledger with source date, access date and limitations
Customer problem baseline and willingness-to-pay evidence
Pre-registered workload, comparator, measurement method and failure-injection plan
Independent reproduction using held-out traces and raw immutable measurements
Costs, regressions, safety limits, uncertainty and reject/no-go recommendation
analyst_control.release_gate: Do not claim solved until an authorized pilot passes its pre-registered criteria and a separate analyst team signs the evidence report.

scope_exclusions: Semiconductor fabrication, packaging/yield and HBM supply-chain capacity: hardware/semiconductor register.
AI model quality, hallucination, agent control, model evaluation and training-data rights: AI/data register. Compute acceptance still protects numerical correctness.
Cybersecurity, IAM policy, vulnerability management, software supply-chain trust and privacy compliance: security register. Here they are constraints, not duplicate sectors.
Database query optimization, data quality, ETL/CDC semantics and data governance: data register; storage mechanisms and distributed transaction boundaries are retained here.
Power generation, utility market reform and water-resource policy: energy/infrastructure register; site compute-power and cooling integration remain explicit cross-references.
Quantum computing, exotic hardware and algorithmic impossibility claims outside the named scope are not covered.
overlap_handling: Do not merge memory bandwidth, memory capacity, tier placement and NUMA locality: they have different controlling variables and tests.
Do not merge ingest, small-object request overhead, SSD wear, archive access and checkpoints: each can be binding while the others are healthy.
Cloud economics is split into use efficiency, allocation, forecasting/commitment, egress, semantic portability, admission and pre-deployment estimation.
Distributed correctness separates quorum safety, side-effect idempotency, overload, time/order, cross-service compensation and cache freshness.
Reliability separates recovery dependency structure, actual restore validation, telemetry economics, diagnosis and change containment.
Developer operations separates build latency, test flakiness, environment determinism, drift, schema evolution, self-service, version skew and routine toil.
